paper_title: Entanglement entropy of a color flux tube in (2+1)D Yang-Mills theory (Amorosso, 2024, JHEP)
deeper_reasoning_1:
\section*{Claim}
For integer \(q\geq2\), the flux-tube observable simultaneously has three paper-critical properties: it is a vacuum-subtracted excess entropy, it is computable as a gauge-invariant Polyakov-loop ratio, and its continuum finiteness is equivalent to a finite nonzero limit of that ratio. More precisely, if
\[
\widetilde S^{(q)}_{|Q\bar Q}(a)=-\frac{1}{q-1}\log R_q(a)
\]
and the source and vacuum Renyi entropies have the same ultraviolet term, then
\[
\lim_{a\to0}\widetilde S^{(q)}_{|Q\bar Q}(a)=S^{(q)}_{f,|Q\bar Q}-S^{(q)}_f
\]
and
\[
\lim_{a\to0}R_q(a)=\exp\left(-(q-1)(S^{(q)}_{f,|Q\bar Q}-S^{(q)}_f)\right).
\]

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & q\in\mathbb Z,\quad q\geq2.\\[1mm]
\text{(P2)} & R_q(a)>0,
\quad \displaystyle \widetilde S^{(q)}_{|Q\bar Q}(a)=-\frac{1}{q-1}\log R_q(a).\\[3mm]
\text{(P3)} & \displaystyle S^{(q)}_{|Q\bar Q}(a)=S^{(q)}_{\rm UV}(a)+S^{(q)}_{f,|Q\bar Q}+r_{Q\bar Q}(a).\\[2mm]
\text{(P4)} & \displaystyle S^{(q)}(a)=S^{(q)}_{\rm UV}(a)+S^{(q)}_{f}+r_0(a).\\[2mm]
\text{(P5)} & \displaystyle \lim_{a\to0}r_{Q\bar Q}(a)=0,
\qquad \lim_{a\to0}r_0(a)=0.\\[2mm]
\text{(P6)} & \displaystyle \widetilde S^{(q)}_{|Q\bar Q}(a):=S^{(q)}_{|Q\bar Q}(a)-S^{(q)}(a).\\[2mm]
\text{(P7)} & \displaystyle P_{\vec z}^{(r)}\mapsto G_{\vec z}^{(r)}P_{\vec z}^{(r)}(G_{\vec z}^{(r)})^{-1},
\qquad \operatorname{Tr}(ABA^{-1})=\operatorname{Tr}(B).\\[2mm]
\end{array}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
First, the common ultraviolet term cancels in the excess entropy:
\begin{align}
\widetilde S^{(q)}_{|Q\bar Q}(a)
&=S^{(q)}_{|Q\bar Q}(a)-S^{(q)}(a) && \text{by (P6)}\\
&=\left(S^{(q)}_{\rm UV}(a)+S^{(q)}_{f,|Q\bar Q}+r_{Q\bar Q}(a)\right)
-\left(S^{(q)}_{\rm UV}(a)+S^{(q)}_{f}+r_0(a)\right) && \text{by (P3),(P4)}\\
&=S^{(q)}_{f,|Q\bar Q}-S^{(q)}_f+r_{Q\bar Q}(a)-r_0(a). && \text{cancellation}
\end{align}
Taking \(a\to0\) gives
\begin{align}
\lim_{a\to0}\widetilde S^{(q)}_{|Q\bar Q}(a)
&=S^{(q)}_{f,|Q\bar Q}-S^{(q)}_f && \text{by (P5)}.
\end{align}
Second, the ratio has the corresponding continuum limit. From (P2),
\begin{align}
R_q(a)
&=\exp\left(-(q-1)\widetilde S^{(q)}_{|Q\bar Q}(a)\right),\\
\lim_{a\to0}R_q(a)
&=\exp\left(-(q-1)(S^{(q)}_{f,|Q\bar Q}-S^{(q)}_f)\right),
\end{align}
using continuity of \(\exp\). Finally, every traced Polyakov factor is invariant because
\begin{align}
\operatorname{Tr}P_{\vec z}^{(r)}
&\mapsto \operatorname{Tr}\left(G_{\vec z}^{(r)}P_{\vec z}^{(r)}(G_{\vec z}^{(r)})^{-1}\right)\\
&=\operatorname{Tr}P_{\vec z}^{(r)} && \text{by (P7)}.
\end{align}
Products, expectation values, ratios, logarithms of positive ratios, and the resulting excess entropy are therefore gauge invariant.

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle
\lim_{a\to0}\widetilde S^{(q)}_{|Q\bar Q}(a)=S^{(q)}_{f,|Q\bar Q}-S^{(q)}_f,
\qquad
\lim_{a\to0}R_q(a)=e^{-(q-1)(S^{(q)}_{f,|Q\bar Q}-S^{(q)}_f)}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_3:
\section*{Claim}
A superselection-sector calculation explains why boundary bookkeeping can drop out of the excess entropy when the static sources do not alter the boundary-sector probabilities. Let
\[
\rho_0=\bigoplus_{k=1}^{m}p_k\sigma_k,
\qquad
\rho_Q=\bigoplus_{k=1}^{m}p_k\tau_k,
\]
with the same sector weights \(p_k\). Then, for \(q>0\), \(q\neq1\),
\[
S^{(q)}(\rho_Q)-S^{(q)}(\rho_0)
=\frac{1}{1-q}\log
\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k^q\operatorname{Tr}(\tau_k^q)}
{\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k^q\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_k^q)}.
\]
Thus no separate classical boundary term survives unless the source changes the sector weights or the sector-resolved quantum traces.

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & \displaystyle \rho_0=\operatorname{diag}(p_1\sigma_1,\ldots,p_m\sigma_m).\\[1mm]
\text{(P2)} & \displaystyle \rho_Q=\operatorname{diag}(p_1\tau_1,\ldots,p_m\tau_m).\\[1mm]
\text{(P3)} & p_k\geq0,
\quad \displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k=1,
\quad \operatorname{Tr}\sigma_k=\operatorname{Tr}\tau_k=1.\\[2mm]
\text{(P4)} & \displaystyle S^{(q)}(\rho):=\frac{1}{1-q}\log\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^q),
\quad q>0,
\quad q\neq1.\\[3mm]
\text{(P5)} & \displaystyle \left[\operatorname{diag}(B_1,\ldots,B_m)\right]^q
=\operatorname{diag}(B_1^q,\ldots,B_m^q)\text{ for positive blocks}.\\[1mm]
\end{array}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
Using block diagonality,
\begin{align}
\rho_Q^q
&=\operatorname{diag}(p_1^q\tau_1^q,\ldots,p_m^q\tau_m^q) && \text{by (P2),(P5)},\\
\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_Q^q)
&=\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k^q\operatorname{Tr}(\tau_k^q) && \text{trace of block diagonal matrix}.
\end{align}
Similarly,
\begin{align}
\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_0^q)
&=\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k^q\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_k^q). && \text{by (P1),(P5)}
\end{align}
Therefore
\begin{align}
S^{(q)}(\rho_Q)-S^{(q)}(\rho_0)
&=\frac{1}{1-q}\log\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_Q^q)
-\frac{1}{1-q}\log\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_0^q) && \text{by (P4)}\\
&=\frac{1}{1-q}\log\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_Q^q)}{\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_0^q)} && \text{log subtraction}\\
&=\frac{1}{1-q}\log
\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k^q\operatorname{Tr}(\tau_k^q)}
{\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k^q\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_k^q)}. && \text{substitution}
\end{align}
If \(\tau_k=\sigma_k\) for every \(k\), the numerator equals the denominator and the excess is zero. More generally, the only surviving terms are the sector-resolved changes inside the same weighted boundary sectors.

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle
S^{(q)}(\rho_Q)-S^{(q)}(\rho_0)
=\frac{1}{1-q}\log
\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k^q\operatorname{Tr}(\tau_k^q)}
{\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k^q\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_k^q)}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_4:
\section*{Claim}
The half-slab cross-cut profile follows from the internal crossing rule once the flux tube has a transverse position distribution. If the half-slab boundary is at transverse coordinate \(x\), the tube is cross-cut with probability \(p(x)\), and a cross-cut creates two fundamental boundary crossings, then
\[
S_{\rm internal}(x)=2p(x)\log N_c.
\]
If \(X\sim\mathcal N(x_0,\sigma^2)\) and cross-cutting means \(X\geq x\), this becomes
\[
S_{\rm internal}(x)=\log N_c\operatorname{erfc}\left(\frac{x-x_0}{\sqrt2\sigma}\right),
\]
which interpolates between \(2\log N_c\) and \(0\) with finite width \(\sigma\).

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & I_x=1\text{ if the flux tube is cross-cut by the half-slab at }x,
\quad I_x=0\text{ otherwise}.\\[1mm]
\text{(P2)} & \displaystyle p(x):=\Pr(I_x=1).\\[1mm]
\text{(P3)} & \displaystyle F_x:=2I_x.\\[1mm]
\text{(P4)} & \displaystyle S_{\rm internal}(x):=\langle F_x\rangle\log N_c.\\[2mm]
\text{(P5)} & \displaystyle X\sim\mathcal N(x_0,\sigma^2),
\quad \sigma>0,
\quad I_x=1\text{ exactly when }X\geq x.\\[2mm]
\text{(P6)} & \displaystyle \Pr(X\geq x)=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{erfc}\left(\frac{x-x_0}{\sqrt2\sigma}\right).\\[3mm]
\end{array}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
The expected number of crossings is
\begin{align}
\langle F_x\rangle
&=\langle 2I_x\rangle && \text{by (P3)}\\
&=2\langle I_x\rangle && \text{linearity}\\
&=2\Pr(I_x=1) && \text{indicator expectation}\\
&=2p(x). && \text{by (P2)}
\end{align}
Therefore
\begin{align}
S_{\rm internal}(x)
&=\langle F_x\rangle\log N_c && \text{by (P4)}\\
&=2p(x)\log N_c. && \text{substitution}
\end{align}
For the Gaussian specialization,
\begin{align}
p(x)
&=\Pr(X\geq x) && \text{by (P5)}\\
&=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{erfc}\left(\frac{x-x_0}{\sqrt2\sigma}\right) && \text{by (P6)},\\
S_{\rm internal}(x)
&=\log N_c\operatorname{erfc}\left(\frac{x-x_0}{\sqrt2\sigma}\right). && \text{substitution}
\end{align}
Since \(\operatorname{erfc}(u)\to2\) as \(u\to-\infty\) and \(\operatorname{erfc}(u)\to0\) as \(u\to+\infty\),
\begin{align}
\lim_{x\to-\infty}S_{\rm internal}(x)=2\log N_c,
\qquad
\lim_{x\to+\infty}S_{\rm internal}(x)=0.
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle S_{\rm internal}(x)=2p(x)\log N_c,
\qquad
X\sim\mathcal N(x_0,\sigma^2)\Rightarrow
S_{\rm internal}(x)=\log N_c\operatorname{erfc}\left(\frac{x-x_0}{\sqrt2\sigma}\right)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_6:
\section*{Claim}
The thin-string model gives a length-difference diagnostic that removes the length-independent internal color baseline and the explicit cutoff factor. For two fully cross-cut flux tubes with the same effective shortest wavelength \(\epsilon\), if
\[
\widetilde S^{(2)}(L)=2\log N_c+\frac{1}{4}\log\frac{L}{\epsilon}+B(L),
\]
then
\[
\widetilde S^{(2)}(L_2)-\widetilde S^{(2)}(L_1)
=\frac{1}{4}\log\frac{L_2}{L_1}+B(L_2)-B(L_1).
\]
Thus the sign and scale of the observed length dependence can be tested without refitting the internal baseline.

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & \displaystyle L_1>0,
\quad L_2>0,
\quad \epsilon>0.\\[1mm]
\text{(P2)} & \displaystyle \widetilde S^{(2)}(L)=2\log N_c+\frac{1}{4}\log\frac{L}{\epsilon}+B(L).\\[3mm]
\text{(P3)} & \displaystyle B(L)\text{ is the residual bounded part of the thin-string entropy}.\\[1mm]
\end{array}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
Evaluate the model at two lengths:
\begin{align}
\widetilde S^{(2)}(L_2)
&=2\log N_c+\frac{1}{4}\log\frac{L_2}{\epsilon}+B(L_2),\\
\widetilde S^{(2)}(L_1)
&=2\log N_c+\frac{1}{4}\log\frac{L_1}{\epsilon}+B(L_1).
\end{align}
Subtracting gives
\begin{align}
\widetilde S^{(2)}(L_2)-\widetilde S^{(2)}(L_1)
&=\left(2\log N_c-2\log N_c\right)
+\frac{1}{4}\left(\log\frac{L_2}{\epsilon}-\log\frac{L_1}{\epsilon}\right)
+B(L_2)-B(L_1)\\
&=\frac{1}{4}\log\left(\frac{L_2}{\epsilon}\frac{\epsilon}{L_1}\right)+B(L_2)-B(L_1)\\
&=\frac{1}{4}\log\frac{L_2}{L_1}+B(L_2)-B(L_1).
\end{align}
If additionally \(|B(L_2)-B(L_1)|\leq\delta\), then
\begin{align}
\left|\left(\widetilde S^{(2)}(L_2)-\widetilde S^{(2)}(L_1)\right)-\frac{1}{4}\log\frac{L_2}{L_1}\right|
\leq\delta.
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle
\widetilde S^{(2)}(L_2)-\widetilde S^{(2)}(L_1)
=\frac{1}{4}\log\frac{L_2}{L_1}+B(L_2)-B(L_1)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$

deeper_metadata.revision_intent: Improve alignment by replacing over-strong modelling claims with conditional derivations that explicitly trace to G1, G2, and G3 while retaining nontrivial synthesis over the core reasoning.

rubric_interpretation.top_level_schema: Exactly paper_title, contiguous deeper_reasoning_k strings, and one deeper_metadata object.
rubric_interpretation.latex_policy: Every deeper_reasoning_k is standalone LaTeX using only article, amsmath, and amssymb.
rubric_interpretation.value_policy: Entries should synthesize multiple core claims into goal-facing diagnostics, not merely restate individual core derivations.

deeper_reasoning_1.title: Unified observable, gauge invariance, and continuum-ratio diagnostic
deeper_reasoning_1.goal_alignment: Directly links vacuum subtraction, gauge-invariant Polyakov-loop ratio, and finite continuum behavior.
deeper_reasoning_1.scientific_payoff: Makes clear that continuum finiteness can be checked either as an entropy limit or as a finite nonzero correlator-ratio limit.
deeper_reasoning_1.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Combines two core proofs into one bidirectional diagnostic for the central observable.
deeper_reasoning_1.formal_sharpness: Conditional theorem with explicit positivity, common-UV, and replica assumptions.
deeper_reasoning_1.low_value_rejection_audit: Avoids merely copying the UV-cancellation proof or the Polyakov-loop proof in isolation.
deeper_reasoning_1.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: Uses the paper-level premise that the Polyakov-loop ratio representation holds; this is declared as an input rather than rederived from the path integral.

deeper_reasoning_2.title: Scoped boundary-prescription invariance
deeper_reasoning_2.goal_alignment: Matches the goals file by proving only the electric-center/trivial-center subfamily claim.
deeper_reasoning_2.scientific_payoff: Shows why source-independent boundary gauge-fixing factors cannot affect the FTE2 ratio.
deeper_reasoning_2.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Converts the robustness narrative into an explicit cancellation calculation.
deeper_reasoning_2.formal_sharpness: States all constants and positivity assumptions explicitly.
deeper_reasoning_2.low_value_rejection_audit: Rejects an over-broad magnetic-center independence claim.
controlled_external_lemmas: cancellation of positive multiplicative constants in a ratio
deeper_reasoning_2.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: Does not assert robustness for uncomputed boundary algebras outside the claimed subfamily.

deeper_reasoning_3.title: Superselection-sector cancellation criterion for excess Renyi entropy
deeper_reasoning_3.goal_alignment: Explains how common boundary-sector weights prevent a standalone boundary Shannon term from polluting the excess observable.
deeper_reasoning_3.scientific_payoff: Separates genuine source-induced sector-resolved changes from boundary bookkeeping effects.
deeper_reasoning_3.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Applies the block Renyi formula comparatively to source and vacuum states.
deeper_reasoning_3.formal_sharpness: Exact finite-dimensional block calculation with common weights declared.
deeper_reasoning_3.low_value_rejection_audit: Avoids claiming all superselection terms always cancel; cancellation requires common sector weights.
deeper_reasoning_3.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: If sources alter boundary-sector probabilities, the result explicitly identifies that as the failure mode.

deeper_reasoning_4.title: Crossing-probability derivation of the half-slab profile
deeper_reasoning_4.target_goal_component: G2 x-dependence and G3 internal-color interpretation
deeper_reasoning_4.goal_alignment: Covers complete, partial, and non-cross-cut regimes and the error-function qualitative model.
deeper_reasoning_4.scientific_payoff: Turns the qualitative finite-width flux-tube picture into a precise crossing-probability formula.
deeper_reasoning_4.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Generalizes deterministic crossing entropy to stochastic half-slab cross-cutting and then specializes to Gaussian deflections.
deeper_reasoning_4.formal_sharpness: Distinguishes the general probability formula from the Gaussian corollary.
deeper_reasoning_4.low_value_rejection_audit: Avoids treating the Gaussian profile as mandatory for all data; it is only a specialization.
deeper_reasoning_4.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: The Gaussian assumption is labelled as a specialization, preserving compatibility with non-Gaussian flux-tube profiles.

deeper_reasoning_5.title: SU(2) fully cross-cut baseline and vibrational positivity test
deeper_reasoning_5.goal_alignment: Matches the goal condition that a fully cross-cut value above 2 log 2 supports a nonzero vibrational component.
deeper_reasoning_5.scientific_payoff: Gives a clear falsifiable threshold for the internal-only model in the SU(2) geometry.
deeper_reasoning_5.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Converts the crossing rule into a continuum-extrapolated diagnostic rather than only a formula.
deeper_reasoning_5.formal_sharpness: Equivalence between positivity of the residual and exceeding the baseline is exact under the additive model.
deeper_reasoning_5.low_value_rejection_audit: Does not claim exact numerical agreement with the full lattice data.
deeper_reasoning_5.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: The conclusion is conditional on the additive interpretation; statistical indistinguishability is not overinterpreted.

deeper_reasoning_6.title: Length-difference diagnostic for the thin-string contribution
deeper_reasoning_6.target_goal_component: G2 length dependence and G3 vibrational interpretation
deeper_reasoning_6.goal_alignment: Connects the reported weak length dependence to the leading logarithmic vibrational prediction.
deeper_reasoning_6.scientific_payoff: Removes the internal baseline and explicit cutoff from length comparisons.
deeper_reasoning_6.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Uses the asymptotic thin-string formula to create a practical difference test.
deeper_reasoning_6.formal_sharpness: Includes the residual term and an optional error bound rather than pretending the leading log is exact.
deeper_reasoning_6.low_value_rejection_audit: Avoids claiming that the paper quantitatively verifies the full thin-string model.
deeper_reasoning_6.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: The residual B(L) is retained explicitly, matching the qualitative rather than exact model-comparison scope.

rejected_low_value_candidates: A separate proof that traced Polyakov loops are gauge invariant without linking it to FTE2; this was absorbed into deeper_reasoning_1.
An unqualified magnetic-center independence theorem; rejected because the goals identify magnetic-center cases as hinted but uncomputed.
A pure restatement of the thin-string Gaussian diagonalization; rejected because the length-difference diagnostic has higher goal payoff.

global_alignment_audit.schema_status: Top-level keys are exactly paper_title, deeper_reasoning_1 through deeper_reasoning_6, and deeper_metadata.
global_alignment_audit.core_coverage: Uses UV cancellation, Polyakov-loop ratio, block-sector Renyi entropy, internal crossing entropy, and thin-string length scaling.
global_alignment_audit.goal_coverage: Covers G1 observable construction and robustness, G2 continuum and half-slab behavior, and G3 internal-plus-vibrational interpretation.

known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: The derivations do not reproduce the full lattice Monte Carlo analysis; they formalize the reasoning structure used to interpret it.
The Gaussian half-slab profile is only one specialization of the crossing-probability formula.
Boundary robustness is limited to the electric-center/trivial-center subfamily specified in the goals.
